title: Vitality overpower NAVI in Katowice group stage thriller
dek: A 13-9 scoreline doesn't tell the whole story of a map that swung three times in the second half.
body: Vitality took down Natus Vincere 13-9 in what was easily the most contested series of the IEM Katowice group stage so far.
NAVI opened strong on the T-side, racing to a 7-2 lead before Vitality's mid-round calling took over. From there, Vitality won 11 of the next 15 rounds to close the map out.
The win keeps Vitality unbeaten in Group A heading into the final round-robin matches.
author: Priya N.

title: VCT Americas Week 4: Sentinels look to extend their lead
dek: Sentinels sit atop the table at 6-1, but NRG and LOUD aren't far behind.
body: Week 4 of VCT Americas kicks off with Sentinels holding a one-map lead over the chasing pack.
NRG's aggressive Fade-Sova composition has been the story of the split so far, and this week's matchup against Sentinels could decide first place heading into playoffs.
author: Priya N.

title: Soul clinch Week 2 top spot with a 21-kill finals day
dek: A dominant final circle in Erangel sealed the top spot for Soul heading into the playoffs push.
body: Soul's aggressive rotation into the final circle on Erangel paid off with a chicken dinner and a combined 21 kills across the day's six matches.
The result puts them narrowly ahead of Global Esports and GodLike in the BGMI Series League Stage standings.
author: Arjun K.

title: Nigma Galaxy's slow-and-steady approach is paying off in PMPL
dek: No individual match wins yet, but consistent top-5 finishes have Nigma Galaxy leading the table.
body: Nigma Galaxy haven't won a single match in PMPL South Asia's League Stage so far, but their placement consistency has them comfortably in first.
It's a reminder that in points-based battle royale formats, survival often beats aggression over a long league stage.
author: Arjun K.

title: Why FRAGGRID covers CS2, Valorant, BGMI and PUBGM — and not more (yet)
dek: A note on scope: we'd rather do four games well than twelve games shallowly.
body: We're launching FRAGGRID with a deliberately narrow lineup: two PC tactical shooters with strong public stats APIs, and two mobile battle royale titles with passionate regional scenes but far less structured data available.

For CS2 and Valorant, match schedules, standings and team data update automatically throughout the day. For BGMI and PUBGM, our team is entering results manually until a reliable commercial data feed exists for those titles — accuracy over false automation.
More titles may come later. For now, this is where we're putting our effort.
author: The FRAGGRID Team
